headline: Last session: Indian benchmarks recorded their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years as Sensex plunged 1,000 points.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 6 October.

why: Global risks from soaring yields on Wall Street
Sustained bearish sentiment leading to an eight-week decline
Technical weakness in Nifty and Sensex benchmarks
whatHappening: Indian equity markets fell for eight consecutive weeks for the first time in 25 years
Approximately Rs 9 lakh crore of investor wealth was wiped out during the recent crash
DLF achieved a total sell-out of its senior living project for ₹1,985 crore
RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das identified five key priorities for India's economic growth
summary: On the last trading day, Indian markets faced a severe downturn with the Sensex crashing 1,000 points amid heavy FII selling. This marked the eighth consecutive week of losses, the longest such streak in 25 years. Investors remain cautious as global cues and high yields continue to pressure domestic equities.
